playbook.intent: An agent is wired straight into one vendor's SDK, and a price change, an outage or a customer's data-residency demand has turned that into a single point of failure. Two months later any step can run on a different provider by configuration alone, a fallback chain covers the primary going down, and the eval bar the single-vendor build met is still being met.
playbook.scope: Move a single-vendor agent (e.g. Anthropic-only) to a portable runtime where Anthropic / OpenAI / local LLM can be swapped per-step or per-tenant, with fallback chain, cost-aware routing, and unchanged eval bar.

success-criteria.criterion: Every model call goes through one interface, so pointing a given step at Anthropic, OpenAI or a local Ollama model is a configuration change and not a code change
The fallback chain has been triggered deliberately, with the primary provider erroring or rate-limiting, and the request still came back in the same shape
The eval suite that guarded the single-vendor build runs unchanged against the portable one, and no score dropped below the bar in force before the move
Per-tenant routing is real: at least one tenant is pinned to a provider other than the default, and the pinning survives a restart
Cost per request is attributed by provider and visible in the observability stack, so cheaper routing can be argued from data instead of intuition
The way back to the single-vendor runtime is written down and has been walked at least once outside production
